items.content_html:
Summary

SQLite does not return disk space to the OS when rows are deleted. With the default auto_vacuum=none, database files grow monotonically regardless of actual data size. This is especially problematic for high-churn databases like Solid Cache, Solid Queue, and Solid Cable — production databases can balloon to many GBs while holding only MBs of real data.

This PR:

  • Adds auto_vacuum: incremental to DEFAULT_PRAGMAS — new databases automatically track freed pages for on-demand reclamation. Existing databases are unaffected (a one-time VACUUM is required to switch modes). Write-only pragmas are skipped on readonly connections.

  • Introduces db:maintenance:vacuum rake task — runs PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(1000) (~4 MB of freed pages) and PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) (resets the WAL file) on all SQLite databases. Warns and skips databases still on auto_vacuum=none. Supports per-database variants for multi-DB apps (e.g. db:maintenance:vacuum:cache). Non-SQLite databases are skipped automatically.

  • Updates guides — documents all 7 SQLite default pragmas in the configuring guide, and adds db:maintenance:vacuum to the command line guide.

The task is designed to be scheduled (e.g. hourly via Solid Queue recurring tasks) for continuous disk space management. A companion PR to rails/solid_queue could add a default entry to config/recurring.yml so new apps get this out of the box.

Context

Rails already sets 6 sensible SQLite defaults (WAL mode, foreign keys, mmap, etc.) but has no protection against unbounded disk growth. The Solid suite amplifies this: Solid Cache expires entries constantly, Solid Queue sweeps finished jobs, and Solid Cable churns WebSocket traffic — all producing freed pages that SQLite never returns to the OS.

There are real-world reports of this problem:

  • Solid Queue #560 — production server ran out of disk space from accumulated finished jobs
  • Solid Cache #116 — maintainer acknowledged no DB-agnostic way to constrain cache storage size

Test plan

  • test_default_pragmas verifies auto_vacuum=2 (incremental) is set by default
  • test_overriding_default_auto_vacuum_pragma verifies override to :full and :none
  • Tests fail without the code change (expects auto_vacuum=2, gets 0)
  • Readonly database tests pass (write pragmas are skipped)
  • SqliteMaintenanceVacuumTest covers incremental vacuum, auto_vacuum=none warning, and WAL checkpoint
  • Full SQLite adapter suite: 94 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors
  • Full SQLite rake suite: 17 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors
items.title: Add SQLite auto_vacuum: incremental default and db:maintenance:vacuum

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

We have a worker's queue in the database.
We would like to fetch a record and mark it as "in progress".
We'd like to avoid a race condition.

Before

  1. Select a few records
  2. Mark one record in the database as in progress
  3. If the record has been marked "in progress" by another process first, then try 2 again with the next record.
  4. If all records were claimed by others, go back to 1 and select a few more.
  5. Return the single record that we were able to claim.

Think we have a few locks thrown in there.

After

  • Select and update a record in one database operation.

Detail

This Pull Request adds update_all_returning.

It leverages Postgres and Sqlite's RETURNING feature to fetch the values in the record updated.

Support

It is not available for MiraDB or MySql.

  • miradb supports RETURNING for insert, but not for update. Had to add a supports_ for this. not thrilled and can change if you prefer.
  • MySql seems to not follow PostgreSQL

I avoided implementing a locking 3 query implementation for MySQL. But I can add something if you prefer. Just felt there are nuances and it would be better for the developer to handle the edge cases.
items.title: Add update_all_returning for atomic update-and-fetch

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Managing credentials currently requires an interactive editor via credentials:edit. This makes programmatic credential management difficult for CI/CD pipelines and AI coding agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, etc.) that cannot interact with $EDITOR.

The credentials:fetch command already supports reading values without an editor, but there is no equivalent for writing or deleting.

Detail

Adds three new subcommands to bin/rails credentials:

# Set or update a credential (nested keys via dot notation)
bin/rails credentials:set aws.access_key_id=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
bin/rails credentials:set stripe.secret_key=sk_live_abc --environment production

# List credential keys (values hidden by default)
bin/rails credentials:list
bin/rails credentials:list --show-values
bin/rails credentials:list --environment production

# Delete a credential (supports subtree removal)
bin/rails credentials:delete aws.access_key_id
bin/rails credentials:delete aws

All commands respect --environment consistent with existing subcommands. No new public Ruby API is introduced.

Additional information

Together with the existing credentials:fetch, credentials can now be fully managed without opening an editor — useful for automated workflows and agent-based development tools that are becoming increasingly common.

Checklist

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why.
  • Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
  • CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature.
items.title: Add credentials:set, credentials:list, and credentials:delete commands

items.content_html:
Refactor PostgreSQL configure_connection to build a hash of all session settings, then set them in a single loop through internal_set_config. This method checks PostgreSQL's parameter_status before issuing SET commands, skipping queries when the server already has the desired value.

Individual settings can be skipped by setting them to false in config, which is useful when connecting through a load balancer or proxy:

production:
  adapter: postgresql
  standard_conforming_strings: false
  intervalstyle: false
  min_messages: false
  schema_search_path: false

For MySQL, wait_timeout can be skipped with wait_timeout: false, and sql_mode can be skipped via variables: { sql_mode: false } (consistent with the existing :default behavior).

Also deprecate set_standard_conforming_strings which is now handled through the consolidated settings hash, and add a parameter_status check to schema_search_path= to skip redundant SET queries.

Related #57013
items.title: Consolidate configure_connection and allow skipping individual settings

items.content_html:
Summary

The ActionDispatch::Reloader middleware (present only when enable_reloading = true, i.e., development) sits inside ShowExceptions in the middleware stack:

Executor → ShowExceptions → DebugExceptions → Reloader → App

The Reloader inherits from Executor, whose rescue block unconditionally reports all exceptions to Rails.error. Because the Reloader is inside ShowExceptions, it reports exceptions before ShowExceptions can decide whether to suppress rescue_responses (404s, 400s, etc.). This causes rescue_responses to be reported to error subscribers in development but silently suppressed in production — a confusing inconsistency.

Changes

Two targeted changes to ActionDispatch::Executor#call:

  1. Rescue block: Skip reporting for rescue_response? exceptions. These are expected HTTP errors (404, 400, etc.) that ShowExceptions will handle — let it make the reporting decision via the existing env flag mechanism.

  2. Response path: Check a new action_dispatch.exception_reported env flag to prevent double-reporting when both the inner Reloader and outer Executor process the same exception.

Behavior after fix

Scenario Reloader reports? Outer Executor reports? Total reports
rescue_response, dev No No 0 ✅
rescue_response, prod N/A No 0 ✅
non-rescue_response, dev Yes No (flag) 1 ✅
non-rescue_response, prod N/A Yes 1 ✅
no ShowExceptions in stack Yes N/A 1 ✅

Benchmark

======================================================================
 Executor Middleware Error Reporting Benchmark
======================================================================

Comparison (before → after):

happy path (no exception):   204.9k → 204.6k i/s  (no change)
rescue_response (404):        23.4k →  25.3k i/s  (+8% faster)
non-rescue_response (500):    23.1k →  23.4k i/s  (no change)

The rescue_response path is faster because it now skips the unnecessary error_reporter.report call.

Fixes #55040
items.title: Don't report rescue_responses from Reloader to error reporter

Motivation / Background

I just created an application with Action Cable and added system tests with Capybara.using_session. The tests hung up because by default, Selenium has only one session per container configured. items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #57061

The default: option on enum silently breaks scoped association .build calls. When building a record through a scoped has_many (e.g., has_many :write_posts, -> { write }), the scope's value is ignored and the record gets the enum default instead.

This is a regression from the old _default: behavior. Since Rails 7.2 stable rejects _default: with ArgumentError, upgrading forces migration to default: which silently introduces this bug.

Detail

Root cause: enum :action, { write: 0, read: 1 }, default: :read calls attribute :action, default: :read, storing the raw symbol :read. Dirty tracking sees this as "changed" compared to the DB column state. In Association#initialize_attributes, "changed" attributes are excluded from scope application, so the scope's value is silently skipped.

Two changes fix this:

  1. activerecord/lib/active_record/enum.rb — Resolve the default: label (e.g., :read) to its mapped DB value (e.g., 1) before passing to attribute(). This makes value_before_type_cast store the integer, not a raw symbol.

  2. activerecord/lib/active_record/associations/association.rb — In initialize_attributes, only treat attributes as "already assigned" if they were explicitly set by the user (differing from the class-level default), not merely defaulted via attribute default:. This ensures scoped associations can override enum defaults during .build.

Additional information

Reproduction script from the issue:

class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :user
  enum :action, { write: 0, read: 1 }, default: :read
end

class User < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :write_posts, -> { write }, class_name: "Post"
end

user = User.create!
post = user.write_posts.build
post.action # => "read" (BUG: should be "write")

Affected versions: Rails 7.0+ through main.

Checklist

  • This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why. If this PR fixes a related issue include it in the commit message. Ex: [Fix #issue-number]
  • Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature.
  • CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.
items.title: Fix enum default: preventing scoped association build from applying scope value

items.content_html:
ActiveJob#retry_on currently accepts Proc values for wait:, but it
rejects other Ruby callables such as Method objects and objects that
implement #call.

This change allows wait: to accept any callable object, while keeping
the existing behavior for proc-based wait handlers.

It also updates the retry_on API docs, adds tests for callable
objects and Method values, and documents the change in the Active Job
changelog.

Example:

class RetryDelay
  def call(executions, error)
    if error.message =~ /retry in (\d+)s/
      $1.to_i
    else
      executions * 2
    end
  end
end

class RemoteServiceJob < ActiveJob::Base
  retry_on CustomError, wait: RetryDelay.new
end

Testing:

AJ_ADAPTER=test bin/test activejob/test/cases/exceptions_test.rb
items.title: Allow retry_on wait to accept callable objects

items.content_html:
FATAL means the server is choosing to terminate the connection, so it's useful for us to clearly distinguish that type of error and correctly translate it to ConnectionFailed instead of general StatementInvalid (which would leave us with a broken connection, to only be noticed later).

I think this could be improved upstream in the pg gem, but our manual result handling is minimal enough that it's also fine to just do it ourselves.
items.title: Report Postgres FATAL exceptions more clearly

items.content_html:
Summary

When running db:migrate on a database that has user tables but is missing
the schema_migrations table, Rails silently loads schema.rb, dropping
and recreating all tables — causing data loss in production.

This happens because initialize_database uses the existence of
schema_migrations as the sole signal for whether a database is initialized.
If that table is missing (manually deleted, database created outside Rails,
legacy app, etc.), it assumes a fresh database and loads the schema.

This PR adds a safety check: before loading schema, verify that no user
tables exist. If they do, raise DatabaseNotManagedError with actionable
guidance instead of silently destroying data.

Fixes #56755.

Changes

  • New error class: ActiveRecord::DatabaseNotManagedError in errors.rb
  • Safety check in initialize_database: Before loading schema, check if
    non-Rails tables exist (anything besides schema_migrations and
    ar_internal_metadata)
  • Optimized: Replaced the original table_exists? call with a single
    conn.tables call that serves both purposes (initialization check + safety
    check), so there is zero performance overhead on the normal migration path

Error message

When triggered, users see:

Unable to migrate database 'my_db': the database already contains tables but
is missing the schema_migrations table. Running db:migrate in this state
would load schema.rb and could destroy existing data. To resolve this,
either run bin/rails db:schema:load if this is a new database, or manually
create the schema_migrations table and register already-applied migration
versions.

Benchmark results

Normal path (schema_migrations exists) — zero overhead:

BEFORE normal (table_exists?):     2857 i/s
AFTER normal (conn.tables):        2898 i/s - same-ish: difference falls within error

Missing path (schema_migrations absent) — same speed:

BEFORE missing (table_exists? only):       2518 i/s
AFTER missing (conn.tables + check):       2440 i/s - same-ish: difference falls within error

Test cases

  1. Raises error when user tables exist but schema_migrations is missing
  2. Does not raise when database is truly empty (no tables)
  3. Does not raise when schema_migrations exists (normal path)
  4. Does not raise when only ar_internal_metadata exists (no user data)

Full ActiveRecord SQLite3 test suite: 9382 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors.
items.title: Prevent db:migrate from destroying data when schema_migrations is missing

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #57042.

When using ActiveStorage's dynamic service resolution (service: ->(record) { ... }), the lambda cannot access the inverse association when building a record through an association with attributes:

class Attachment < ActiveRecord::Base
  belongs_to :user, inverse_of: :attachments
  has_one_attached :file, service: ->(record) { record.user&.eu? ? :eu_storage : :us_storage }
end

# Works — build first, assign later:
attachment = user.attachments.build
attachment.file = { io: StringIO.new("data"), filename: "test.txt" }

# Broken — user is nil when the service lambda runs:
attachment = user.attachments.build(file: { io: StringIO.new("data"), filename: "test.txt" })

Root Cause

Inside ActiveRecord::Core#initialize, the execution order is:

  1. assign_attributes(attrs) — triggers the dynamic service lambda
  2. yield self (block) — initialize_attributes → set_inverse_instance sets the inverse

The inverse (record.user) is set in step 2, but step 1 already needed it.

Solution

In Association#build_record, pass only STI type attributes (if any) to klass.new, then inside the block:

  1. set_inverse_instance(record) — inverse available immediately
  2. record.assign_attributes(attributes) — attribute setters can access the inverse
  3. initialize_attributes(record, attributes) — scope/FK protection runs last

This preserves:

  • STI class resolution — type attribute is still passed to new for proper subclass instantiation
  • Foreign key protection — initialize_attributes runs after assign_attributes and overwrites any user-provided FK with the correct scope value
  • Through association FK — through_association.rb handles nil attributes when adding source FK

Benchmark Results

CPU (iterations/second, Ruby 4.0.1):

Scenario Before (main) After Delta
build no attrs 20,206 i/s 19,862 i/s same-ish
build with attrs 17,143 i/s 17,302 i/s same-ish
build nested 19,737 i/s 20,392 i/s same-ish
build STI 14,696 i/s 15,272 i/s same-ish

Memory (allocations per call):

Scenario Before After Delta
build no attrs 61 61 identical
build with attrs 71 71 identical
build nested 64 64 identical
build STI 80 80 identical

Zero performance regression on both CPU and memory.

Checklist

  • Tests added for has_many and has_one inverse availability during build
  • Full ActiveRecord sqlite3 test suite passes (9,380 runs, 0 failures)
  • STI, FK protection, polymorphic, and through association tests pass
  • RuboCop clean
  • CHANGELOG entry added
  • Benchmarked before and after (CPU + memory)
items.title: Set inverse before attribute assignment in association build

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #57042

When using parent.children.build(attributes) with a model that has an ActiveStorage attachment with a dynamic service (e.g., has_one_attached :file, service: ->(record) { record.parent.region_service }), the service proc fails because the parent association is nil at the time the attachment attribute setter runs.

This happens because ActiveRecord::Core#initialize calls super (which triggers assign_attributes) before yielding the block that sets the inverse instance via initialize_attributes.

Detail

The fix has two parts:

  1. ActiveRecord::Core#initialize — yield the block before calling super (which triggers assign_attributes). This ensures that initialize_attributes (which sets the inverse instance and foreign key) runs before user-provided attributes are assigned.

  2. Association#build_record — move the user-provided block (yield) outside of build_association so it runs after both initialization and attribute assignment. This preserves the existing behavior where blocks passed to build can override attribute values.

Additional information

Verified with 2,289 tests across all association types, STI, nested attributes, autosave, callbacks, persistence, scoping, eager loading, and ActiveStorage — zero new failures introduced.

Checklist

  • This Pull Request is related to one change.
  • Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why, with issue reference.
  • Tests added to verify the inverse is set before attributes are assigned during build.
  • CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. (N/A — bug fix)
items.title: Fix association build to set inverse before assigning attributes

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Fixes #56780

When preloading associations where the key column has a case-insensitive collation (SQLite NOCASE, MySQL _ci, PostgreSQL citext or non-deterministic ICU collations), the database correctly returns matching records but the preloader fails to associate them back to their owners. This is because owners_by_key is a plain Ruby Hash with case-sensitive key lookup — "Home" and "home" are different keys in Ruby even though they match in the database.

This affects all association types (belongs_to, has_many) with CI string key columns, including composite keys.

Solution

1. Add Column#case_sensitive? to the base Column class (default true), with adapter-specific overrides:

  • MySQL: Already had this method (!collation.end_with?("_ci")) — no changes needed
  • SQLite: Returns false for NOCASE collation
  • PostgreSQL: Returns false for citext type and non-deterministic collations (detected via pg_collation.collisdeterministic, added to the existing column_definitions query with zero extra DB round-trips)

2. Normalize keys in the preloader when the key column is case-insensitive:

  • Cache a case_insensitive_key? boolean at init time
  • In convert_key, downcase string keys only when the flag is set
  • For composite keys, track which indices need normalization via ci_key_indices
  • Zero overhead on the common case-sensitive path

Benchmark Results

1,000 owners, 1,000 records, Ruby 4.0.1:

Case-sensitive path (common case — most users):

Metric Original New Overhead
Single key build+lookup 2,826 i/s 2,985 i/s 1.06x faster
Composite key build+lookup 1,517 i/s 1,442 i/s 1.05x slower
Single lookup only 10.3M i/s 10.0M i/s same-ish
Memory (build + 1000 lookups) 68,872 bytes 68,872 bytes identical

Case-insensitive path (bug fix — was returning nil before):

Metric New (fixed) Note
Single key build+lookup 2,115 i/s Original was broken (nil)
CI memory 148,872 bytes +80KB from String#downcase (unavoidable)

Testing

  • SQLite: 4 preloader tests (belongs_to CI, has_many CI, composite key CI, case-sensitive control) + 3 collation case_sensitive? tests
  • PostgreSQL: 2 tests (citext, plain string)
  • Base Column: 1 test (default true)
  • Full activerecord suite: 9,010 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors
  • RuboCop: 0 offenses
items.title: Fix preloader to respect case-insensitive column collations

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This rails new command can fail during run_solid when a customized generation flow (Rails application template, generators, etc.) includes solid_queue/solid_cable but omits solid_cache.

run_solid currently invokes a fixed command sequence (solid_cache:install solid_queue:install ...) without checking whether each gem is actually present in the generated app. In template/custom app generator workflows, this can raise:

Unrecognized command "solid_cache:install" (Rails::Command::UnrecognizedCommandError)

This bug was discovered while creating a custom app generator (template-based flow), which can produce the same partial Solid setup.

Detail

This Pull Request changes run_solid to install Solid components individually and only when their gem is declared in Gemfile.

Changes included:

  • Refactor run_solid to run per-component installers instead of one hard-coded combined command.
  • Add regression test for template/customization scenario where solid_cache is removed from Gemfile but other Solid gems remain.
    • Add coverage for all combinations of:
      • solid_cache
      • solid_queue
      • solid_cable
    • Add explicit test for --skip-action-cable interaction.

Additional information

This change is intentionally defensive for template-driven/custom generator flows (rails new -m ...) where Gemfile can be modified before run_solid executes.

With default rails new behavior, all Solid gems are present unless --skip-solid is used. However, template/customization workflows can produce partial Solid configurations and should not fail generator execution.
items.title: Refactor solid installation commands and add tests for gem configuration

items.content_html:
Motivation

Fixes #56861

Since Rails 7.1 runs after_commit callbacks in definition order, user callbacks defined after has_one_attached/has_many_attached can't see attachment_changes — Active Storage's callback deletes the entry via .delete before user callbacks run.

class User < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_one_attached :avatar
  # Active Storage registers: after_commit { attachment_changes.delete("avatar").try(:upload) }

  # This callback runs AFTER the delete — attachment_changes["avatar"] is nil!
  after_commit :process_avatar, if: -> { attachment_changes["avatar"].present? }
end

Solution

Preserve attachment changes in previous_attachment_changes before clearing them during upload. Similar to Active Record's previous_changes, this gives user callbacks a reliable way to check what changed:

class User < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_one_attached :avatar

  after_commit :process_avatar, on: %i[create update],
    if: -> { previous_attachment_changes["avatar"].present? }
end

previous_attachment_changes is cleared on reload and initialize_dup, matching the lifecycle of attachment_changes.

Performance optimization

Also replaces .try(:upload) with respond_to?(:upload) + direct .upload call, eliminating the overhead of .try's internal respond_to? + public_send chain.

Benchmark Results

Speed: create attachment (common path)

ORIGINAL: .delete.try(:upload):       3,092k i/s  (323 ns/i)
NEW: delete + ivar + respond_to:      4,190k i/s  (239 ns/i)  — 1.36x FASTER

Speed: delete attachment (edge case)

ORIGINAL: .delete.try(:upload):       4,174k i/s  (240 ns/i)
NEW: delete + ivar + respond_to:      4,175k i/s  (240 ns/i)  — same

Memory (100 iterations)

Old: 20,000 bytes (200 objects)
New: 36,000 bytes (300 objects) — +16KB per 100 commits (one extra hash entry)

Test Plan

  • Test: previous_attachment_changes available in after_commit (has_one)
  • Test: previous_attachment_changes available in after_commit (has_many)
  • Full attached model tests: 0 regressions (153 runs, same failure count as main)
  • RuboCop passes
  • Benchmarked: 1.36x faster than original on common path, same on edge case
items.title: Add previous_attachment_changes for after_commit callbacks

items.content_html:
Motivation

Fixes #56876

When ssl_mode is set in database.yml (common with the Trilogy adapter for caching_sha2_password), db:schema:dump fails because mysqldump on Debian/Ubuntu is not compiled with --ssl-mode support:

mysqldump: unknown variable 'ssl-mode=required'

Solution

Detect at runtime whether mysqldump/mysql supports --ssl-mode by checking its --help output. If supported, the flag is included (backward compatible). If unsupported, it is skipped and a warning is logged.

The detection is memoized per command via a class-level method MySQLDatabaseTasks.ssl_mode_supported?.

Backward compatibility

  • mysqldump with --ssl-mode support (MySQL 8.0+): flag included as before, zero behavior change
  • mysqldump without --ssl-mode support (Debian/Ubuntu): flag skipped, warning logged, dump succeeds
  • No ssl_mode in config: no detection runs, zero overhead

Benchmark Results

Tested against real MySQL 8.0 (Docker) with both ssl-mode-supporting and simulated Debian mysqldump.

Detection overhead

Cold detection:  ~3ms (shell out to mysqldump --help)
Memoized:        ~0ns (hash lookup, 35,000x faster)
Runs once per task invocation.

Full flow verification

Debian mysqldump WITH --ssl-mode:    exit=1 FAIL (the bug)
Debian mysqldump WITHOUT --ssl-mode: exit=0 SUCCESS (our fix)

Detection for Debian mysqldump:  false (correctly skips)
Detection for MySQL 8.0:         true  (correctly includes)

Memory

Detection (100 calls): 2,492,200 bytes (600 objects)
Memoized (100 calls):  0 bytes (0 objects)

Other adapters

  • PostgreSQL: Not affected — uses PGSSLMODE environment variable, not CLI flags
  • SQLite: Not affected — no SSL

Test Plan

  • Test: ssl_mode included when mysqldump supports it (trilogy)
  • Test: ssl_mode skipped when mysqldump doesn't support it (trilogy)
  • Test: ssl_mode included when mysqldump supports it (mysql2)
  • Test: ssl_mode skipped when mysqldump doesn't support it (mysql2)
  • RuboCop passes on all changed files
  • Full-flow benchmark against real MySQL 8.0
  • Verified Debian-like mysqldump fails without fix, succeeds with fix
items.title: Skip unsupported --ssl-mode in mysqldump/mysql CLI

items.content_html:
Motivation

Fixes #56950

When using dependent: :detach (or manually detaching), blobs become unattached but should remain available for a grace period before purging. The existing purge advice uses created_at, which means blobs attached for years and then detached are immediately purged — they appear "old" because created_at reflects when the blob was uploaded, not when it became unattached.

Solution

1. Add dependent: :detach option

has_one_attached and has_many_attached now accept dependent: :detach. When the record is destroyed, the attachment record is removed but the blob and its file on the service are preserved.

class User < ApplicationRecord
  has_one_attached :avatar, dependent: :detach
end

Valid dependent options are now validated: :purge_later, :detach, or false. Invalid values raise ArgumentError.

2. Add updated_at to active_storage_blobs

A nullable updated_at column is added to the blobs table. The blob is touched when:

  • An attachment is explicitly detached (user.avatar.detach)
  • An attachment is destroyed via record destroy with dependent: :detach

The touch only fires for dependent: :detach — not for dependent: false where the user explicitly opted out of cleanup behavior.

DetachMany uses touch_all for a single batch UPDATE ... WHERE id IN(...) instead of N individual touches.

3. Updated purge guide

The recommended purge task now uses COALESCE(updated_at, created_at) instead of created_at:

ActiveStorage::Blob.unattached.where(
  "COALESCE(active_storage_blobs.updated_at, active_storage_blobs.created_at) <= ?",
  2.days.ago
).find_each(&:purge_later)

Benchmark Results

Migration Impact

Adding nullable updated_at column is a metadata-only operation
on PostgreSQL (instant) and MySQL (instant for nullable without default).
No table rewrite needed. Zero downtime.

Touch Callback Overhead (single blob)

blob.touch (UPDATE updated_at):     4,998 i/s  (200 μs/i)
blob.reload (SELECT, baseline):     7,282 i/s  (137 μs/i)
Touch is 1.46x slower than a SELECT — but only runs once per detach.

Batch touch_all vs N individual touches (DetachMany)

 1 blob:  touch_all 1.60x faster
 5 blobs: touch_all 6.62x faster
10 blobs: touch_all 12.54x faster
50 blobs: touch_all 43.45x faster

Memory: 50 blobs, 100 iterations

N individual touches: 123,272,440 bytes (1,009,952 objects)
Single touch_all:       2,283,100 bytes (24,200 objects)    — 54x less memory

Purge Query Comparison

WHERE created_at <= ? (old):                          3,481 i/s
WHERE COALESCE(updated_at, created_at) <= ? (new):    3,883 i/s
Same query plan. COALESCE adds no overhead.

Test Plan

  • Test: dependent: :detach keeps blob on has_one record destroy
  • Test: dependent: :detach keeps blobs on has_many record destroy
  • Test: blob updated_at is touched when attachment is detached
  • Test: blob updated_at is NOT touched for dependent: false
  • Test: DetachMany touches blobs in a single batch query
  • Test: ArgumentError raised for invalid dependent options
  • Test: reflection shows :detach dependent for has_one and has_many
  • Full Active Storage test suite: 0 regressions
  • RuboCop passes on all changed files
  • Benchmarked: migration, touch overhead, batch touch_all, purge query, memory

items.content_html:
Motivation

Fixes #57027

Fixes flaky CI failures caused by the connection pool reaper thread interfering with test lifecycle.

Two distinct failure modes:

1. False-positive leak detection (PostgreSQL)

RuntimeError: Found 1 leaked connection after
BelongsToAssociationsTest#test_belongs_to_counter_after_update
owner: #<Thread:... "AR Pool Reaper" sleep>

The reaper's checkout_for_maintenance temporarily leases connections. If check_connection_leaks runs at that moment, it flags the connection as leaked.

2. Trilogy::SynchronizationError (MySQL/Trilogy)

Trilogy::SynchronizationError: This connection is already in use by another thread or fiber

The reaper's preconnect/keep_alive accesses raw Trilogy sockets from its background thread while the test thread uses the same connection during pin_connection!/unpin_connection!.

Root Cause

Both are race conditions between the reaper's background maintenance cycle and the test lifecycle (setup_transactional_fixtures, pin_connection!, unpin_connection!, check_connection_leaks).

Solution

Two-part fix:

1. Disable the reaper on test connection pools (test/support/config.rb)

Set reaping_frequency: 0 for all test database configs. This prevents the reaper thread from spawning for the main test pools, eliminating both race conditions at the source.

Reaper behavior is independently tested in reaper_test.rb with dedicated pools that set their own reaping_frequency.

2. Safety net in check_connection_leaks (test/cases/test_case.rb)

Acquire pool.reaper_lock before checking for leaks, in case any test creates a pool with reaping enabled. This ensures maintenance connections have been returned before we inspect them.

Reproduction

The race condition was reproduced locally by simulating checkout_for_maintenance from a background thread:

=== Simulating reaper race condition ===
Results: 100/100 detected false-positive leaks (100.0%)
Race condition REPRODUCED!

=== Testing fix: pool.reaper_lock { } ===
Results with fix: 0/100 false positives (0.0%)
Fix WORKS!

Test Plan

  • Connection pool tests pass (149 tests, 0 failures)
  • Reaper tests pass (9 tests, 0 failures) — they use their own pools
  • test_belongs_to_counter_after_update passes
  • RuboCop passes on changed files
  • Race condition reproduced and verified fixed locally
items.title: Fix flaky test failures caused by connection pool reaper
